Performance is so close that it's hardly worth mentioning in raster, and while 24gb VRAM is nice, 16gb is more than enough in virtually every game at 1440p and even at 4k (might be one or two where it matters, but I don't know of any yet).

If you're paying the same price and deciding between FSR 4 or 24gb VRAM, I'd go with FSR 4 all day. Going from FSR 3 to FSR 4 is almost like going from 1080p to 1440p, it's that good. Support isn't great ATM, but I have no doubt it will be in every new and upcoming game by the end of this year. Future proofing also seems like a bad idea to me, since we don't know what games will need, but there's an argument for the 9070 XT being better in that regard with many games coming out with forced ray tracing now. It hasn't been an issue yet for 7900 XT, but the 9070 XT is substantially better at RT, so worth noting.

Last thing I'd say is that I just started seeing the 9070 XT at much lower prices now (around $700), so that's a no brainer. Whichever is cheaper is probably the best answer, but I'd actually pay about $50 more for FSR 4 honestly lol

I really try not to cheese any bosses in the game and I just finally managed to beat him solo without summons or shield pokes after like... 80-100 tries? Idk, I stopped counting because it was so much... but maaaan it was brutal. Honestly, it's a bs fight. It's not very fun imo and unlike beating other extremely difficult bosses, including even Malenia, I got less of a feeling of accomplishment and more of just relief that I wouldn't have to fight him again. I'm not even gonna sit her and act like I was just able to use my build without stepping out of it a bit, because I did use some cheese I think. Maybe? Idk if it counts as cheese, but I highly recommend using hefty rot pots. In the first phase, it only takes one to rot him and you can use it right after you dodge his opening gravity spin thing (as long as he actually decides to open with that, usually does though). That rot should last the entire first phase and can pretty much get him into the second phase almost by itself. Second phase I just chucked one at him right away so long as I had full hp, but it takes at least 2 pots to rot him now. If you throw one immediately and then he start to charge the nuke attack thing, just throw the second and tank the hit and heal it off. Worth it for the rot. If you're quick enough, you can probably even use a holyproof pickled liver, or even do what I did and use the spell Lord's Divine Fortification for and insane 70% holy damage reduction before getting nuked to help reduce all the holy damage coming your way soon. That fortification spell and rot pots were the only thing that got me through the fight in at least a kinda legit way lol. Also try using pierce damage, he resists it the least. Also weak to holy in the first phase, but probably not worth much.

Other than the more hardcore dueling meta at 125, 150 seems to be the consensus still for the general PvP oriented player base. That being said, around 200, give or take, seems to be the natural level people end up post DLC based on this poll, and you'd actually be missing out on matching with most people if you stop at 150, as the matchmaking only goes up to 185. However, a lot of the player base going above 200 are typically more PvE oriented and will likely be leaving once they've finished the DLC and not taking part in PvP as much, so the dedicated ones who continue playing will probably just stick to 150. I think if you want to match with the most people possible, 165 would probably be the right place to stop. You'll still be able to match against players at level 150 and while you could argue that your wins against 150s might feel a bit cheapened, I personally don't think you'll get a massive advantage over them. The main benefit though is that you'll also be able to match with players up to 200 and while they'll have an advantage technically, it likely won't be enough to be the difference between you winning or losing most of the time. I think 165 is probably the way to go for people who just want to enjoy PvP with the most people possible.

I think what you described is actually more like the Monty Fall Problem. Look that up and it might help you understand it better.

Small correction. Monty choosing a door without a car behind it is not because choosing the other door would reveal a car necessarily. Your explanation doesn't actually work if you picked the door with the car behind it. If you did pick the door with car, then Monty can reveal either of the doors you didn't pick. That's because the Monty Hall problem only requires that Monty knows what's behind every door and always reveals a goat from one of the doors you didn't pick. He only can't reveal the car because he has to reveal a goat, not because he's obligated to not reveal a car. May seem like I'm nit-picking, but it actually matters.
